text:
anya: Quick thread to flesh out the micro-peering + edge-proxy idea w/ emphasis on ephemeral vs reserved egress. keeping notes here.
marco: +1. summary: create regional peering attachments per-tenant when sustained traffic crosses a threshold; tear down when idle. optional paid pin for static egress.
devon: Need to nail scale limits early. per-account peering quotas, route table entry scaling, and peering acceptance IAM flow are the main blockers.
lia: Also think about route table size per-VPC. If every peering adds routes, we blow up route tables and cause convergence slowness.
anya: Proposal details:
  - Controller watches tenant throughput window and connection churn.
  - If throughput > PEER_CREATE_HWM for N minutes -> create peering + attach route + provision tiny edge-proxy (could be multi-tenant process w/ per-tenant SNAT rules).
  - If peer unused for PEER_IDLE_TTL -> mark for teardown (grace window for pinned flag).
marco: Implementation variants:
  A) One peering per tenant into shared regional edge VPC. pros: clean src-ip, simple routing. cons: peers per account skyrockets.
  B) Shared peering pool: small number of peerings per account, route-steering via proxy. pros: fewer objects. cons: proxy adds latency and complexity.
sam: Small note: cross-account peering requires either automated accept from tenant side (we own both sides for some customers) or a signed webhook for acceptance. we should support both flows.
devon: Observability / alerts we need: per-region peering_count, attach_rate, detach_rate, route_ops_per_min, peer_create_failures, md_pmtu_errors, snat_mismatch_events. infra-bot: quota_notification: peering_count=47 region=eu-central-1 threshold=48 
lia: Security model: limit route propagation to only CIDR prefixes we expect, tag routes with tenant-id, and insist on explicit security-group allowlist on edge-proxies. avoid broad LR rules.
anya: Edge-proxy behavior: terminate TLS, validate tenant certificate, optionally do SRCIP pass-through. If proxy handles >1 tenant, use kernel-level SNAT table per-tenant to avoid conntrack explosion.
marco: Ops lifecycle concerns: attach/detach churn for high-churn tenants could cause route table thrash. mitigation: add backoff hysteresis + keep warm pool of N spare peerings per-region.
devon: Cost modeling asks: generate per-tenant monthly cost for scenarios: low-churn pinned (1 RPS sustained), bursty many small tenants (100ms bursts), and mid-tier (10 RPS sustained). include API create costs and proxy VM hours.
lia: Customer-facing SLA: if pinned/reserved-egress accepted, guarantee stable egress IP for billing period. ephemeral peering will have a best-effort window (e.g., 24h before static IP lost on teardown) that must be documented.
anya: Pseudo lifecycle controller: 
```
on metric_tick(tenant):
  if tenant.rps > PEER_HWM and not tenant.has_peer:
    ensure_peer(tenant)
  if tenant.has_peer and tenant.idle_for > PEER_IDLE_TTL:
    schedule_teardown(tenant)
```
marco: Test plan:
  - unit: simulate attach/detach logic, route tagging cleanup.
  - integration: create 200 peering attachments in a scratch account and measure route table convergence and describe time-to-attach.
  - chaos: kill edge-proxy to validate fallback to hosted-relay.
sam: Fallback path must be seamless: if peering fails, route traffic to hosted-relay and flag in metrics. customers won't tolerate request errors during peering churn.
devon: IAM automation: need a short-lived role that can accept peering for tenant accounts OR a one-time token flow during signup. record audit logs and allow tenant revocation.
lia: Danger: transitive peering is not supported. designs that assume multi-hop will break. every tenant path must be direct into regional edge or fall back to relays.
anya: Action items: 
  - @marco: run the 200-peering integration in staging and capture attach/teardown latencies.
  - @devon: build quota spreadsheet and escalation template for AWS service limits.
  - @lia: write short security checklist: route tag invariants + SG rules + audit plan.
  - @sam: prototype proxy SNAT table per-tenant (linux iptables/nft rules) and measure conntrack.
  - infra-bot: wire peering_count alarms to #eng-sre and create dashboard.
infra-bot: alert_stub: peering_count=60 region=us-east-1 threshold=55 notify=[@marco,@devon]
marco: I'll start the spike tomorrow morning, will post results here. initial expectation: micro-peering helps predictable customers, but we need robust heuristics to avoid scaling costs for many small customers.
anya: Great. Let's keep this thread as the coordination point. If anyone wants to riff on heuristics or edge cases, drop notes here. :rocket:
